title: introduce-economy-rules-engine-prefetch-presets-and-unit-econ-cli
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Product teams want safer automated defaults that reduce per-token cost without manual tuning. This change introduces a lightweight rules engine (Economy Rules) that synthesizes batching/prefetch defaults and quantization candidate profiles from recent traffic signals and unit-economics targets. It also adds a developer CLI (unit-econ-snap) to preview cost/latency tradeoffs for a route before applying defaults. The design aims for conservative opt-in defaults with automatic safety rollback and an audit trail for private deployments.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds EconomyRules service, prefill and kv-cache presets generator, quant-profile selector, a preview CLI (unit-econ-snap), runtime hooks for safe rollout/fallbacks, telemetry labels for unit-econ experiments, docs and e2e tests.

Checklist:
- [x] EconomyRules protobuf and service implementation
- [x] Prefetch/prefill policy generator (runtime + config)
- [x] QuantProfile selector with safe candidate scoring and fallback whitelist
- [x] unit-econ-snap CLI to simulate route-level unit economics locally
- [x] Telemetry: new metrics and tags (econ.profile, econ.reason)
- [x] Tests: unit + integration + smoke against small perf canary
- [x] Docs: user guide and migration notes

Design notes: EconomyRules is implemented as a pluggable micro-service inside the Optimize component. It consumes anonymized route telemetry (latency histogram, token distribution, cache-hit rate, recent model variants) and a customer target (e.g., per-1k-token cost budget or latency SLO) to emit a ranked list of candidate defaults: batching.window_ms, batching.max_batch, prefill.enabled, prefill.prefill_size, kv_cache.policy (none/partial/full), and quant.profile (int8/4-bit/default-quant). Each candidate gets a conservative score combining estimated cost delta, P95 latency delta, and regression risk score computed from historical evals. By default the platform applies only the top candidate as a suggested default; admins can opt-in to auto-apply. For private installs, the service runs in the control plane and writes suggested presets to the customer's config store with an audit log.

Safety and rollback: every applied change is tagged with an epoch id and a safety window. The runtime monitors per-route quality regressions and P99 spikes; if an alert threshold is exceeded the system automatically reverts to the previous stable preset and emits an incident annotation. The quant-profile selector includes a conservative whitelist of models that support low-bit quantization; unsupported models are automatically filtered.

unit-econ-snap CLI: A developer can run `unit-econ-snap simulate --route <route> --window 1h --budget 0.08` which fetches recent telemetry (or uses a local CSV), runs the EconomyRules scoring engine in a sandbox, and prints a ranked JSON of candidates with estimated unit-econ impact and simulated latency histograms. CLI supports `--apply` to push a suggested preset to a dev namespace only.

Telemetry & observability: new metrics: econ.suggest.count, econ.apply.count, econ.rollback.count, econ.candidate.latency_delta_ms, econ.candidate.cost_delta_per_1k. Added dashboard panels under Redwood Console > Optimize > Economy Rules showing distribution of applied presets and rollback reasons.

Backward compatibility & migration: Existing routes retain their explicit configs. EconomyRules only targets routes with `defaults: auto-suggest` set in route config. Default behavior for all customers is 'suggest-only'. Migration docs describe how to enable auto-apply for Dedicated and Private.

Security/privacy: only aggregated/anonymized telemetry is read by default for hosted accounts. Private installs use on-prem telemetry. No raw user prompts or payloads are sent to the service.

Testing and validation: ran perf canary across two fleets (small/medium) for 72 hours. Observed median token-cost reduction of 12% on synthetic conversational traffic without hitting P95 latency SLO. E2E tests validate CLI flows and rollback behavior.

Rollout plan: staged rollout over three waves: (1) internal dev tenancies, (2) opt-in beta customers, (3) opt-out default for non-regulated customers after 8 weeks and additional regression checks.

Related: integrates with ENG-7124 (unit-econ targets) and ENG-7160 (prefill telemetry), support ticket SUP-908 requested route-level cost preview CLI for enterprise SREs.

review_discussion:
Arjun: please clarify how candidate scoring weights are chosen and whether they're exposed to customers.
Maya: weights are internal heuristics tuned from historical workloads; for hosted accounts weights are fixed but we surface the estimated cost/latency deltas. For private installs we expose a 'weight override' flag in the config but default remains conservative.
Lucie: needs explicit unit tests for the rollback trigger.
Maya: added focused tests for rollback condition and simulated regression in tests/e2e.
Samir: quantify the perf impact of the CLI when sampling telemetry — is it safe for large routes?
Maya: CLI uses sampling + bounded window; default operation is a dry-run that doesn't fetch full payloads. Added `--sample-rate` flag and documented limits.
Arjun: approving once telemetry labels are in place.
Lucie: approved after a test flake fix.
release_notes: Adds Economy Rules service (experimental), unit-econ-snap CLI for previewing cost/latency tradeoffs, conservative prefill and quantization preset suggestions, and automatic safety rollback. Default mode: suggest-only. See docs/optimize/economy-rules.md for migration and opt-in steps.
